body:
_Migrated from issue #1001, filed 2026-07-19._

Split out of #1000 (cross-family review finding).

## What

Three places download build artifacts over HTTPS with no integrity check:

- `Dockerfile`, `pbs_upstream` stage — the python-build-standalone tarball
- `Dockerfile`, `kepubify_upstream` stage — the kepubify binary
- `scripts/ensure-python-mirror.sh` — the same two artifacts, when it *builds* the GHCR mirror

HTTPS authenticates the transport, not the artifact. A truncated, swapped, or tampered download becomes the Python interpreter baked into the image.

## Why it is not urgent

- The shipped image is unaffected today: every CI image build pins `PBS_SOURCE=ghcr`, and the mirror is a content-addressed registry pull.
- The `*_upstream` stages are the contributor path, so the exposure is a contributor's local build.
- It matches what the Dockerfile already does for lsof and calibre, which are also unverified downloads. This is a pre-existing gap that the fallback inherits rather than a new one.

## What to do

Pin per-architecture SHA-256 hashes next to the version pins in the Dockerfile's global ARG block, verify them in both `*_upstream` stages (`sha256sum -c`), and have `ensure-python-mirror.sh` check the same hashes before publishing a mirror tag — one source of truth, so the mirror cannot be built from an artifact the Dockerfile would reject.

Forgetting to bump a hash alongside a version pin then fails the build loudly, which is the safe direction. Worth extending to the lsof and calibre downloads in the same pass.
title: Verify checksums on the Python and kepubify downloads
